thread.title: Town OKs higher water, sewer rates
thread.title_full: Town OKs higher water, sewer rates

author: ohtadmin
title: Town OKs higher water, sewer rates
text:
The price to furnish public water and treat its subsequent sewage is getting more expensive for households in the utility district.
The town council, sitting as the water and sewer commissioners, approved the budgets for fiscal year 2026-27 at its Aug. 17 meeting.
The operating budget on the wastewater side increased $65,675, or 6.4%, from $1.02 million to $1.09 million. This budget will require a 6.8% increase in the flat usage rate from $22.02 to $23.51 per 1,000 gallons each quarter.
The operating budget for the water department increased $86,967, or nearly 4.4%, from $2 million to $2.08 million. This budget requires 10% increases for both excess water and the quarterly minimum fee.
To meet the increases, the quarterly minimum fee for water has increased from $124.98 to $137.48, raising the average annual bill from $500 to $550. This fee includes the first 5,000 gallons of water used per quarter.
Homeowners who conserve and remain at this level will see their annual combined bills, including state surcharges and sewage fees, increase 6.5 percent from $1,228 to $1,308, or about $6.67 per month.
Customers connected to public water, after that initial 5,000 gallons, will see a 10% increase for metered excess water with rates increasing from $12.14 to $13.36 per 1,000 gallons used in the 8,000-gallon per quarter/32,000- gallon per year tier; from $13.05 to $14.36 in the 13,000/52,000 tier; from $16.54 to $18.19 in the 16,000/64,000 tier; from $23.01 to $25.31 in the 32,000/128,000 tier; from $28.23 to $31.06 in the 68,000/272,000 tier; from $36.14 to $39.76 in the 169,000/676,000 tier; and from $45.99 to 50.59 in the 210,000/840,000-gallon tier.
Finance Director Tina Collins said the annual water increase to households is between 6.5% and 10% based on the tiered structure of gallons used.
The total increase, including state surcharges and sewage fees, for the average homeowner on the 13,000/52,0000 tier is about 6.6%, from $2,566 to $2,735, or $14 per month.
Town Administrator Ed Mello cited multiple reasons for the increases. First, Dish Network filed for bankruptcy and is no longer paying its lease to store telecommunications equipment on the water tower.
Mello also elected to transfer $75,000 from the fund balance rather than $100,000 like last year.
“We’re trying to wean ourselves away from relying on the fund balance,” he said.
The cost for sludge disposal increased 25% from $28,000 to $35,000 while the cost of insurance skyrocketed 134%, from $15,000 to $35,060. State-mandated testing, moreover, rose 20%, or $3,000.
Salaries and benefits for the water department increased 5.7% to $385,656 and 5.2% to $543,083 on the wastewater side.
The approved budget also ups fees, which have “not been touched in a long time,” Mello said. The fee to turn service on or off increased from $100 to $300. The fee to install or remove service also was raised $200.
The cost for new connections to the water or sewer systems was increased $2,000 from $3,000 to $5,000.
“The current rates have been here for a very, very, very long time,” Mello said. “It’s an access fee. You don’t get anything else but access to the system.”
The commissioners also endorsed Mello’s plan to charge contractors with paying for state inspectors. If a contractor gets a permit to open a state road, for example, Mello said, an inspector must be hired.
“We, the municipality, are responsible for paying that state inspector who sits there,” he said. “So, we had no method of collecting that. We would have to go to the contractor and ask them to pay that. We’re changing that process to where we are collecting that fee up front so we are certain that fee is paid and the municipality is not out of pocket paying it.”

Homeowners who conserve and remain at this level will see their annual combined bills, including state surcharges and sewage fees, increase 6.5 percent from $1,228 to $1,308, or about $6.67 per month. Finance Director Tina Collins said the annual water increase to households is between 6.5% and 10% based on the tiered structure of gallons used.
